messages:
maya: Quick UX check — thinking about a 'compact' mode for the Audit Log nav so the roles matrix and audit pages line up better when screen width is <1200px. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz — wireframes in frame 'Audit / Compact'

luke: I like compact for power users. Two immediate asks: keep keyboard jump (g then l) and ensure breadcrumbs don't disappear on scroll. :thumbsup:

sanjay: agree re keyboard. also compact rows need higher contrast on hover — current grey is too subtle for accessibility. maybe #E6EDF3 -> #DCEAF8

ana: copy nit: onboarding toast says "Audit view condensed" — suggest "Compact audit navigation" to avoid confusion with condensed table rows.

olivia: question: how does this affect Invite flow? When you click "View audit" from an invite card, does it open the compact nav or full nav? I think it should match user's preference (remember toggle).

maya: plan is preference-driven toggle per account, default to full for new orgs. For invites, open contextually (if user is in compact, open compact). Does that make sense?

luke: sounds right. tiny layout nit — when compact is on, the roles matrix header gets cramped. Could we collapse role pills under a single + menu at <900px?

sanjay: +1, and ensure screen reader announces collapsed state: "Roles collapsed, 3 items". Add aria-expanded on the pill container.

ana: accessibility checklist: keyboard focus visible on row, focus order preserved when collapsing, aria-labels on the toggle, and test with NVDA/VoiceOver.

design-bot: deploy mock to staging: /staging/audit-compact. Run lightweight ax tests and post results.

maya: thanks—I'll update figma with the collapsed pills and copy tweak, then put a 1-hour sync tomorrow 11:30 for final signoff. Everyone ok with that? :eyes:
